# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 33 LORNA RETURNS

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Two weeks afterward Lorna Vane returned by herself to the ancient residence where she had passed a great number of painful years. During the June dusk she crossed the fields toward Nell’s place, and materialized with the suddenness of a ghost inside the fragrant garden.
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0000 }

“Lorna!” Nell exclaimed, astonished. “From where did you suddenly appear? Your arrival was completely unknown to us. What kept you from writing? A meeting at the station would have been arranged for you.”
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0001 }

“Somehow I was unable to write, Nell. Trying to express anything using a pen and ink felt completely useless. Besides, returning silently and without attracting attention was what I desired.”
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0002 }

Nell wrapped her arms around Lorna and planted a kiss on her. Lorna affectionately returned the embrace. Looking washed out and exhausted, she uttered a soft sigh while sinking onto the grass next to a massive patch of daffodils, which shone amid the faint, silver-hued dusk like stars of gold.
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0003 }

“And did you return to your home by yourself, Lorna?”
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0004 }

“Yes. Laurence Vane’s sister arrived in Montreal and brought him back home with her. Poor guy, he regretted leaving me—even though he didn't know me when his memory began to return. He held onto me during those initial difficult days as he attempted to understand that Rufus’s death had not happened just yesterday, as he felt it had. The whole situation was extremely tough on him. I gave him as much assistance as I was able to. His sister's arrival made things simpler for him, since he felt like he had just seen her a short time ago. Luckily she looked much the same, which served to aid him as well.”
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0005 }

“It is completely peculiar and marvelous, Lorna. I believe not one of us comprehends it as yet.”
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0006 }

“I am unable to. Sixty minutes ago, when I stepped inside that house across the way, I had the sensation that it HAD to be a dream—that Rufus had to be present, displaying his innocent grin, just as he was for such a lengthy time. Nell, I still appear to be numb. I am neither joyful nor sorrowful—nor ANYTHING at all. My sensation is that a piece of my existence was abruptly ripped away, leaving a dreadful void. My sensation is that I cannot be myself—as though I have transformed into a different person and am unable to adapt. A terrifyingly solitary, confused, and powerless sensation comes over me. Being with you once more brings comfort—it feels like you serve as a kind of anchor holding my wandering spirit. Oh, Nell, every bit of it fills me with fear—the rumors, the surprise, and the inquiries. Considering that makes me desire that my return home had never happened. Dr. Dave waited by the station as I stepped from the locomotive—he drove me to my house. The unfortunate old fellow suffers greatly since he informed me a long time back that no remedy existed for Rufus. 'I genuinely believed that, Lorna,’ he uttered to me this very day. 'However, I ought to have advised you against relying on my judgment—I ought to have advised you to consult a expert. Had I done so, you would have been spared numerous painful years, and poor Laurence Vane numerous squandered ones. I hold myself deeply at fault, Lorna.’ I instructed him to refrain from that—he acted according to what he believed correct. He has constantly shown such goodness to me—I was unable to tolerate seeing him distress himself about the matter.”
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0007 }

“And Rufus—I mean Laurence? Has he completely recovered his memory?”
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0008 }

“For the most part. Naturally, numerous particulars still escape him—though his memory recovers further with each passing day. The night following the burial of Rufus, he stepped outside to take a stroll. Carrying Rufus’s watch and funds, he intended to return those items to me, together with the letter I wrote. He acknowledges visiting an establishment frequented by seamen—and he recalls consuming alcohol—and that is all. Nell, the instant his own identity returned to him is something I will always remember. His gaze met mine, filled with a wise yet confused look. I inquired, ‘Do you know me, Rufus?’ To which he replied, ‘I never saw you before. Who are you? And my name is not Rufus. I am Laurence Vane, and Rufus died of yellow fever yesterday! Where am I? What has happened to me?’ I—I lost consciousness, Nell. And from that point on, it has seemed to me as though I am living in a dream.”
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0009 }

“It will not take you long to adapt to this altered situation, Lorna. Moreover, you possess youth—a lifetime lies ahead—and numerous wonderful years remain for you.”
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0010 }

“Maybe I will manage to view it like that after some time, Nell. At this moment I am too exhausted and unconcerned to ponder the future. I am—I am—Nell, I am lonely. I long for Rufus. Isn’t it entirely very odd? Do you know, I was genuinely attached to poor Rufus—Laurence, I guess I ought to say—exactly as I would have been attached to an incapacitated child who relied on me for every single thing. I would not ever have confessed it—I was actually embarrassed by it—since, you see, I had abhorred and detested Rufus so intensely before he departed. When I learned that Captain Saul was transporting him back home I anticipated I would simply harbor the identical feelings toward him. But I never did—even though I kept on despising him as I recalled him previously. From the moment he arrived home I experienced merely compassion—a compassion that pained and distressed me. I assumed at that point that it was simply since his mishap had rendered him so incapacitated and altered. But currently I think it was since a truly distinct individual was present there. Carlo was aware of it, Nell—I realize now that Carlo was aware of it. I constantly considered it odd that Carlo had not recognized Rufus. Canines are typically so loyal. But HE recognized it was not his owner who had returned, even if not one of the others among us did. I had not ever observed Laurence Vane, you know. I recall at present that Rufus one time noted in passing that he possessed a cousin in Nova Scotia who resembled him as closely as a twin; but the matter had slipped from my mind, and regardless I would not ever have considered it of any significance. You see, it never crossed my mind to doubt Rufus’s identity. Every alteration in him appeared to me simply the consequence of the mishap.
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0011 }

“Oh, Nell, I will always remember that April evening when Hugh informed me of his belief that Rufus could be healed! It felt as though I had previously been confined inside a gruesome cage of torment, only for the entrance to be unlocked so I could emerge. Though still tethered to the cage, I was no longer trapped within. Yet during that night, a feeling came over me that a cruel force was dragging me backward into that cage—back toward an agony far more horrific than what I had previously suffered. Hugh was not at fault in my eyes. I believed his judgment was correct. Moreover, he acted with great kindness—stating that should I choose against taking the risk, given how costly and unsure the surgery was, he would hold no grudge against me whatsoever. Even so, the proper choice was clear to me—yet I lacked the courage to confront it. Throughout the entire night, I paced back and forth like a lunatic, attempting to force myself into confronting it. I was unable to, Nell—I believed it was beyond my power—and as dawn arrived, I clenched my jaw and determined that I WOULD NOT. Things would be allowed to stay precisely as they were. My actions were deeply sinful, I admit. Had I simply been forced to live with that choice, it would have served as fair retribution for such sinfulness. For the duration of the day, I stuck to my resolve. Later that afternoon, some errands required me to travel up to the Glen. Because it happened to be one of the calm, sleepy days for Rufus, I departed without leaving anyone with him. My trip lasted slightly past my expectations, causing him to notice my absence. A sense of solitude came over him. Upon my return to the house, he rushed toward me exactly as a youngster would, displaying an expression of immense delight. In that moment, Nell, I simply broke down. Enduring that look upon his pitiful, empty face proved to be beyond my strength. A feeling struck me that I was withholding from a child the opportunity to mature and evolve. Regardless of what the outcome might turn out to be, I recognized my duty to grant him his opportunity. Consequently, I walked over and informed Hugh. Oh, Nell, during those weeks prior to my departure, my behavior must have struck you as abominable. That was never my intention—yet my mind could focus on nothing other than my obligation, while all surrounding things and people seemed like mere phantoms.”
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0012 }

“I am aware—I comprehended, Lorna. And at present it has all finished—your fetter is snapped—no enclosure exists.”
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0013 }

“No cage exists,” Lorna said again distractedly, her slim, tan hands picking at the fringe of grass. “However—it feels like nothing else is there, Nell. You—you recall what I shared with you regarding my foolishness that evening on the sand-bar? It seems a person fails to recover from being foolish rapidly. At times I believe certain individuals remain fools eternally. And being a fool—in that manner—is nearly as terrible as being a—a dog attached to a chain.”
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0014 }

“When your fatigue and confusion pass, your perspective will change greatly,” stated Nell, who refrained from bestowing excessive pity because she was aware of a particular fact that Lorna was ignorant of.
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0015 }

Lorna rested her magnificent head of gold upon the knee of Nell.
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0016 }

“At all events, YOU are mine,” she stated. “Existential emptiness is impossible alongside a companion like that. Nell, stroke my head—in the exact manner you would for a small girl—give me some MATERNAL affection—and allow me to convey, while my obstinate tongue is momentarily freed, precisely what you and your fellowship have signified to me ever since the night of our meeting on the rocky coast.”
{: #nw-v04-c33-p0017 }
